clue.text: Sweet farm animal I dressed in fancy suit

indicators.note: the animal and I are clothed by the suit, so they sit inside its letters
fancy as in elaborate or fanciful, telling us the letters of suit are rearranged

parts.note: a ram is a male sheep, a farm animal

explanation.surface: A sheep and the speaker are kitted out in an elaborate costume.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fancy' makes TISU and 'dressed in' wraps it round the animal and I; 'Sweet' looks like an adjective but is the noun for a dessert.
explanation.definitionFit: Tiramisu is an Italian dessert, so it is an example of a sweet.

clue.text: Platform by the sea's as rickety in the end

parts.note: qua is a Latin-derived word meaning 'as' or 'in the capacity of'

indicators.note: only the final letter of the word rickety is wanted

explanation.surface: A seaside platform is described as wobbly at its far end.
explanation.definitionFit: A quay is a landing stage or wharf built at the water's edge for boats.

clue.text: Jack's replaced head of tool: it blocks signals

indicators.note: the opening letter of the tool is swapped out for the Jack letter

parts.note: a hammer is a tool
J is the card abbreviation for jack

explanation.surface: Someone called Jack has fitted a new head to a tool that interferes with radio.
explanation.definitionFit: A jammer is a device transmitting interference that stops radio or phone signals getting through.

clue.text: Knight, south of sunken area, spies Spanish city

indicators.note: in a down answer, being south of something means coming below it

parts.note: a vale is a valley, low-lying ground
N is the chess notation for knight
the CIA is the US intelligence agency

explanation.surface: A knight positioned below a valley watches spies in a Spanish city.
explanation.definitionFit: Valencia is a major port city on Spain's east coast.

clue.text: Brother returning sauce bottles has sweetener

indicators.note: the brother and the sauce hold another piece inside them, as a bottle holds liquid
the word for the sauce is read backwards

parts.note: ragu is an Italian meat sauce
to own something is to have it

explanation.surface: A brother coming back with bottled sauce has something to sweeten it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'returning' gives UGAR and 'bottles' holds the word for has inside; 'sauce bottles' reads as a noun phrase but 'bottles' is a verb.
explanation.definitionFit: Brown sugar is a partly refined cane sugar used to sweeten food.

clue.text: Vigour of compilers primarily liking deception

parts.note: setters refer to themselves as we, so compilers gives WE

indicators.note: only the opening letter of liking is taken

parts.note: a lie is a deception

explanation.surface: Puzzle setters' energy comes mostly from enjoying trickery.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Give it some welly' is British slang for putting real effort in, so welly or wellie means vigour.
explanation.definitionFit: Informal British slang sense: welly, also spelt wellie, means power or energetic effort.

clue.text: Criminal must lie, covering up a sham

indicators.note: the jumbled letters wrap round the single letter, hiding it within
criminal suggests something crooked, so the letters are bent out of order

explanation.surface: A crook has to tell lies to conceal a fraud.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Criminal' rearranges MUST LIE into SIMULTE, which 'covering up' wraps round A.
explanation.definitionFit: To sham is to fake or pretend, the same verb sense as feigning something.

clue.text: Praises sex changes, receiving flipping good deal

indicators.note: the rearranged letters take in another piece, holding it inside
changes signals the letters of sex being altered in order
the word for a good deal is turned over, read backwards

parts.note: a lot means a good deal, a large amount

explanation.surface: Someone who undergoes a sex change gets an unexpectedly generous settlement and is praised.
explanation.walkthrough: 'changes' gives EXS, and 'receiving' takes in TOL, which 'flipping' makes.
explanation.definitionFit: To extol is to praise highly, so the third-person form matches 'praises'.

clue.text: Broadcast Mass in French for people in service

parts.note: to air something is to broadcast it
M is the physics symbol for mass
en is the French word for in

explanation.surface: A Mass celebrated in French is broadcast for those serving.
explanation.definitionFit: Airmen are members of an air force, people serving in the armed services.

clue.text: Axes keep paint evenly off the wall

indicators.note: the axes hold the picked letters inside them

parts.note: z and y are names of axes on a graph

indicators.note: the second and fourth letters of paint are taken

explanation.surface: Someone tells axes to keep paint off the wall uniformly.
explanation.walkthrough: Axes on a graph are labelled x, y and z, so two of those letters enclose the even letters of paint.
explanation.definitionFit: Off the wall is an idiom for bizarre or eccentric, just like zany.

clue.text: Look after water supply in Scottish club

parts.note: to mother someone is to look after them
a well is a source of water

explanation.surface: Someone tends to the water supply at a Scottish club.
explanation.walkthrough: Motherwell is a town in Scotland whose football club plays in the Scottish top flight.
explanation.definitionFit: Motherwell FC is a professional Scottish football team, so it is an example of a club.

clue.text: Orca about 45 inches back in the drink

indicators.note: the reversed measure is placed inside the drink

parts.note: kir is a drink of white wine and blackcurrant liqueur

indicators.note: the measure is read backwards

parts.note: an ell is an old measure of cloth, around 45 inches

explanation.surface: A killer whale roughly 45 inches long swims back into the sea.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The drink' is slang for the sea, which suits an orca, but here it is the cocktail KIR, which takes LLE.
explanation.definitionFit: Orcas are commonly called killer whales, so killer is a shortened name for one.

clue.text: Ultra harsh, after trashing final performance

indicators.note: trashing wrecks the words, so their letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Critics savage a farewell show with ultra harsh reviews.
explanation.definitionFit: A last hurrah is an idiom for a final effort or appearance before retiring.

clue.text: Way to march forwards on pitch, then sulk on the way back

parts.note: locks are forwards in a rugby team's second row

indicators.note: the word for a sulk is read in reverse

parts.note: a pet is a fit of sulking, as in 'in a pet'

explanation.surface: Instructions for a parade: advance on the field, then sulk going backwards.
explanation.walkthrough: In rugby the locks are second-row forwards.
explanation.definitionFit: Lockstep is marching close behind one another with feet moving in unison.

clue.text: Not in wrong camp

parts.note: out can mean mistaken, as in 'your figures are out'
a side is a faction or camp in a dispute

explanation.surface: Someone excluded finds themselves in the wrong camp.
explanation.definitionFit: Being outside means being not in, located beyond the interior.

clue.text: Drivel in legal document is shown to be wrong

indicators.note: the drivel sits inside the legal document

parts.note: a deed is a legal document
bunk means nonsense or drivel

explanation.surface: Nonsense in a legal paper is exposed as false.
explanation.definitionFit: Debunked claims have been exposed as false, i.e. proven mistaken.

clue.text: Criticise lightweight's characterful text

parts.note: to pan a show is to criticise it harshly
a gram is a very small unit of weight

explanation.surface: A reviewer slates a flimsy author's colourful writing.
explanation.definitionFit: A pangram is a sentence using every letter of the alphabet, so it is full of characters.

clue.text: Decent English queen caught in a tryst

indicators.note: the English queen is trapped within the other pieces

parts.note: a date is a romantic meeting

explanation.surface: A respectable English queen is caught out in a romantic assignation.
explanation.definitionFit: Adequate means satisfactory or acceptable, the sense of decent as 'good enough'.

clue.text: Severe Conservative dismissed by press

indicators.note: the party abbreviation is sent away from the word for press

parts.note: to constrict is to squeeze or press tightly

explanation.surface: A harsh Tory politician is fired by the newspapers.
explanation.definitionFit: Strict and severe are synonyms, both meaning harsh and uncompromising.

clue.text: Literary captain stores record and French letters

indicators.note: the captain keeps the record within him

parts.note: Ahab is the captain in Moby-Dick
an LP is a long-playing record
et is the French word for and

explanation.surface: A fictional captain keeps a record and some condoms.
explanation.walkthrough: 'French letters' is British slang for condoms, but 'French' belongs with 'and'.
explanation.definitionFit: The alphabet is the full set of letters used to write a language.

clue.text: Bit of muslin in glove?

indicators.note: only part of the run of letters across these words is wanted

explanation.surface: A scrap of fine cotton tucked into a glove.
explanation.definitionFit: A piece of muslin inside a glove would serve as its inner layer, so the whole clue defines it.

clue.text: Edging in front of brown Fiat

indicators.note: only the opening letter of brown is taken

parts.note: a fiat is an authoritative decree or order

explanation.surface: Trim on the front of a brown Fiat car.
explanation.walkthrough: Fiat looks like the Italian car maker; here it is a decree.
explanation.definitionFit: A border is an edging round something, like the trim on a garment.

clue.text: Super computer's menu choice

parts.note: big can mean great or super
a Mac is an Apple computer

explanation.surface: A supercomputer's options list.
explanation.definitionFit: The Big Mac is McDonald's signature burger, a familiar item to order.

clue.text: Disobeying one far-right group going around

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one
NF is the National Front, a British far-right party
ringing means encircling or going round

explanation.surface: A lone extremist faction is roaming about in defiance of the law.
explanation.walkthrough: The National Front is a British far-right party.
explanation.definitionFit: Infringing a rule means breaking it, which is a form of disobedience.

clue.text: Herb said to make basis for sauce

indicators.note: said tells us the word is spoken, giving a word with the same sound

parts.note: rue is a bitter herb

explanation.surface: A herb is reputed to be the foundation of a good sauce.
explanation.definitionFit: A roux is flour cooked in fat, the base for thickening sauces.

clue.text: Run and charge around in rocky area

parts.note: R is the cricket abbreviation for run

indicators.note: the word for a charge is turned round

parts.note: a fee is a charge for a service

explanation.surface: A runner charges about in rough, rocky ground.
explanation.definitionFit: A reef is a ridge of rock or coral near the water's surface.

clue.text: Nice one! Pro on lake is to remove bindings

indicators.note: in an across answer, one piece on another means it follows it

parts.note: un is French for one, as spoken in the city of Nice
an ace is an expert or pro

explanation.surface: Praise for a professional on a lake who must take off their ties.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Nice' is the French city, not the adjective, so its 'one' is UN.
explanation.definitionFit: To unlace is to undo laces, freeing what they tie together.

clue.text: Artist very cutting in short farce

indicators.note: the artist and very slice into the word for short

parts.note: short-tempered means testy
RA is a Royal Academician, an artist

explanation.surface: A very sharp artist intervenes in a brief comedy.
explanation.definitionFit: A travesty is an absurd, distorted imitation, a sham or mockery like a farce.
